calls.head: The Penguins get in close, the Blackhawks shoot from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Pittsburgh is the league’s best, but Chicago is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Blackhawks handle the Penguins
paras: Connor Bedard played his first game of the season, after missing the first six, and picked up an assist. Teuvo Teräväinen got the scoring started for the Blackhawks 28 seconds in. Sidney Crosby tied it midway through the first. Roman Kantserov gave the Blackhawks the lead on the power play late in the first. Kantserov struck again midway through the second to make it 3-1. Nick Robertson made it 3-2 late in the second. Crosby scored his second of the night midway through the third to tie it 3-3. Teräväinen scored his second of the night with 4:18 left to put the Blackhawks ahead for good. Tyler Bertuzzi added the empty-netter with 10 seconds left to make it 5-3. Teräväinen also had an assist.

The Penguins had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Penguins win about six in ten. Spencer Knight made 24 saves for the Blackhawks, and Sergei Murashov stopped 15 of 19.
The Blackhawks killed all four Penguins power plays. The Hawks improved to 2-5-0, and the Penguins dropped to 3-3-1.

items.text: Bryan Rust’s point streak against Chicago ended after at least five games.
Sidney Crosby scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Apr 5.
The Blackhawks bounced back after two straight losses.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
